explanation: Environment prepared and the full reference executed offline under the controller. Dependency-only pyproject pins MDAnalysis==2.11.0, MDAnalysisTests==2.11.0, pandas==3.0.6 and matplotlib==3.11.2 for the base image's CPython 3.13.13; 31 packages resolved and installed with no system packages needed (MDAnalysisTests ships only an sdist, but it is pure Python and built fine without compilers). stage-inputs.sh stages the notebook's PSF/DCD/CRD inputs as byte-identical copies under /inputs (primary source: the installed MDAnalysisTests package data; fallback: the sha256-pinned mdanalysistests-2.11.0.tar.gz PyPI sdist) and verifies them with sha256sum -c; the controller confirmed the 3 staged files were still byte-identical after the offline run. The offline reference ran in 2.7 s at 162 MiB peak with MPLBACKEND=Agg (set by the controller), exit 0, and produced all three reviewed endpoint CSVs with the exact frozen export code: rmsd_core_ca_atomgroup.csv (4134 B, sha256 dc413717...), rmsd_mass_weighted.csv (9534 B, 20841677...), rmsd_custom_weighted.csv (9506 B, 55d28d1e...); declared_artifacts_present: true. Content is sane and reproducible: 98 trajectory frames each, frame-0 RMSDs ~1e-07 Å, and my separate probe of the untouched original.py against the same input bytes gave matching values (e.g. CORE max 1.9677980 Å, mass-weighted C-alpha max 6.8334149 Å, custom-weighted NMP max 13.9263352 Å). One reference test was consumed and it passed on the first attempt; no changes to imports, exports, selections, parameters or branches were made.
source_adaptations: analysis.py inserts 8 immediately-adjacent lines (a 6-line explanatory comment plus three single assignments PSF=/DCD=/CRD=) directly after the untouched 'from MDAnalysis.tests.datafiles import PSF, DCD, CRD' import. Reason: that import resolves the three input paths inside the read-only installed MDAnalysisTests package data, which is not a persistent, controller-verified offline input location; the same bytes are re-declared and staged under /inputs and hash-checked byte-identical (96cec916... adk.psf, 859a5bd9... adk_dims.dcd, cd7f5e20... adk_open.crd; verified against both the installed package data and the pinned PyPI sdist mdanalysistests-2.11.0.tar.gz, sha256 5edeb5b0...). The import statement itself and all of its bindings remain intact and unmodified; no algorithm, selection, weight, parameter or narrative change was made.
Plot rendering runs headless via the controller-set MPLBACKEND=Agg environment variable; no plotting call, figure or axis code was altered, so all original plotting behaviour is preserved.

No dependency was added beyond what the notebook declares (MDAnalysis, MDAnalysisTests, pandas) plus matplotlib, which the notebook's presentation directive [%matplotlib inline] and the retained pandas .plot(...)/set_ylabel(...) calls require; matplotlib unwraps to the Agg backend in this environment.
unresolved_assumptions: Data redistribution review is still 'not yet established' per the preparation record: the AdK PSF/DCD/CRD files are MDAnalysis' distributed test data (LGPL-2.1 project), but biological inputs and generated bundles should stay private until a separate licensing/redistribution check clears them.

The controller's own semantic-fidelity validation flag is false (it reported semantic_fidelity_validated: false); this run demonstrates completion, artifact presence and input-byte invariance, not independently verified numerical correctness or suitability as a grading benchmark. The reported CSV values are corroborated only by my separate execution of the untouched original.py against the same input bytes.

Wheel-level platform specificity was not fully characterised: the resolved linux x86_64 wheels and the QCP Cython kernels were validated only on this sandbox's x86_64 CPU (AVX-512 present) with CPython 3.13.13; a different architecture or interpreter could select different builds, though MDAnalysis 2.11.0 publishes CPython-3.13 x86_64/aarch64 manylinux wheels.

The exported tables are only the three terminal DataFrames that survive to script completion; the open-vs-closed backbone RMSD (unnamed discarded expression) and the whole-Universe backbone/CORE/LID/NMP table (overwritten in df) are excluded per the reviewed plan and cannot be exported from live variables.
